title: Convergent or divergent: does an endless sum stop growing?
examples: What is the difference between convergent and divergent?
Why does the harmonic series diverge?
Do shrinking terms always give a finite sum?

explain.say: Here are two endless sums. Both add smaller and smaller pieces. Do both stop growing? Your guess might surprise you. Look at the left side: 1 plus a half plus a quarter, halving each time.

draw.text: Convergent or divergent: does an endless sum stop growing?

draw.verdict: Shrinking pieces are not always enough

explain.say: Each piece halves, so they shrink very fast. The total creeps up to 2 and settles there. A sum that settles on a number is called convergent. Can you see why it can never pass 2?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Shrinking pieces are not always enough

explain.say: Now the right side: 1 plus a half plus a third plus a quarter. This is the harmonic series. The pieces still shrink, but slowly. Does it settle too?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Shrinking pieces are not always enough

explain.say: No! Group the pieces: a third plus a quarter is more than a half. The next four pieces, a fifth to an eighth, are more than a half again. You can always make another half, so the total grows past any number. It diverges.

draw.verdict: Shrinking pieces are not always enough

explain.say: Well done, that one fools a lot of people! It grows very slowly though: you need 12367 terms just to pass 10. Mathematicians in 14th-century France already knew this trick.

faq.q: What is the difference between convergent and divergent?
faq.a: A convergent series settles towards one fixed total. A divergent series does not: it grows without end, or keeps jumping around.

faq.q: Why does the harmonic series diverge?
faq.a: Group its terms: one third plus one quarter is more than a half, the next four terms are more than a half, the next eight are more than a half, forever. Endless halves make an endless total.

faq.q: Do shrinking terms always give a finite sum?
faq.a: No. The terms must shrink to zero for a sum to converge, but that is not enough. They must shrink fast enough, like halving.
asks: If the terms go to zero, does the series converge?

faq.q: How slowly does the harmonic series grow?
faq.a: Very slowly. You need 4 terms to pass 2, 31 terms to pass 4, and 12367 terms to pass 10.

faq.q: Who proved the harmonic series diverges?
faq.a: Nicole Oresme in France gave the grouping proof around 1350. It was proved again later by Pietro Mengoli and the Bernoulli brothers.
asks: Who discovered the harmonic series diverges?

facts: The partial sums of the harmonic series first exceed 10 after 12 367 terms.

quiz.show: Why is "terms shrinking to zero" not enough for a series to converge?
